cells.tense: The weight is in your hands right now and the decision is moving with it.
cells.act: keep the connection coherent while it is hard
cells.ask: When a hard moment comes with someone, don't leave and don't fix it. Just stay beside them and keep talking plainly until it passes.
cells.core:
You carry what has to be carried and you put it where it belongs, and the ones standing on what you've set down don't have to check it. Nobody tells you it holds; you can see it holding by how they stand on it. That isn't a small thing. Most people can build something that lasts. You can build something that lasts and keep your hands off it.

There's a person in your life who trusts you with the hard version of themselves — the part that isn't settled yet. Stay beside them while it's moving. Don't solve the feeling; just be there with them and keep talking plainly. Connection like that is an equal exchange. You give steadiness; you get to see what it holds up.
cells.sheetLine: What you build holds, and they can stand on it.

cells.tense: You will have already built the whole outcome out ahead of the people living it.
cells.act: make the fair call about a feeling, yourself
cells.ask: Next time a feeling rises in you, wait a day before acting on it. Then weigh it with the same measure you'd hand anyone else.
cells.core:
Where you carry weight, the plan is already finished in your head before anyone gets to start it. You know how it should go, and you've mostly worked it out ahead of time — and the working-out is where the strain lives now. The ones who lean on you can feel the floor go hard under them. Holding slides into forcing.

Before the next thing you've already decided, give the feeling a day. Set the raw reaction aside, wait, then weigh it fairly — not loosely, not harshly. The same measure you'd give anyone else. That's what your hands know how to do, just aimed at yourself for once. The grip eases, and the person beside you gets to move again.

cells.tense: You were already at the door, and you keep standing there explaining it.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what is not
cells.ask: Take one finished thing you're still defending and set it down. Don't argue for it again; let it stay finished without you.
cells.core:
In the weighing, the weight you carried is nearly weightless now. You look for the thing that's out of proportion and find nothing there — no scale to read and nobody asking you to be steady. There isn't a load to pick up, and you keep walking back to where the old one used to sit. What you built before is holding somewhere, and you aren't in it.

Somewhere you did complete cleanly, and you're still hauling it around, making the case for it. That finished thing can come down. Don't argue for it again. The hands take a minute to remember ease. What's still unfinished is worth keeping; what's done can go quiet. That's how the energy comes back to a place that can't hold it.

cells.tense: Your steadiness is already holding the room together and your name isn't on it.
cells.act: start something for the spark of starting
cells.ask: Begin something with no purpose past the beginning of it — a page, a meal, a walk somewhere aimless. Keep at it a few days.
cells.core:
Where you balance things, the correction is already happening through you and you don't count it as yours. When something's off, you feel it and you put it back level, and then you leave it alone — no ceremony, no note that you did it. The fairness runs through your hands. What isn't running is the part where you get to want things for yourself.

Begin one thing that isn't for anyone, for no reason past the beginning. A page, a meal, a walk somewhere aimless. Keep at it a few days, so it sits on the record with a name attached. It won't fix the room, and it isn't meant to. You get to hear what your own reach sounds like when it's the thing moving.
